title: Panama Disease of Banana
content:
Fusarium wilt of banana, better known as Panama disease. It is one of the major diseases of banana due to which the farmer can suffer hundreds of losses. Fusarium oxysporum fsp cubense  is caused by the attack of the fungus. Disease spread The fungus is soil borne i.e. it stays in the soil. Bacteria can survive for a long time as dead organisms on plant residues. Bacterial survival depends on soil moisture, texture and acidity. Germs spread through saplings or saplings. Bacteria can easily enter the roots through damaged roots. The attack and spread of the disease is faster if the worm attacks the roots of the banana plant. Once the organism enters the plant, it spreads to all parts of the plant through transport tissues. **Symptoms** are : 
1. At first, light yellow spots appear from the lower edge of the old leaves of the affected plant. The yellow spots move towards the midveins of the leaves and turn dark brown, and the leaves eventually dry up
2. Later the upper leaves also start turning yellow
3. Affected leaves break off and droop near the plant
4. Suddenly the entire plant or 2/1 leaves may drop
5.  Bhuakand bursts longitudinally
6. If the stems and roots are cut crosswise, reddish-black spots can be seen in the alimentary canal

title: Ash gourd disease?
content: Ash gourd (Benincasa hispida), also known as winter melon or wax gourd, is a large,, nutrient-dense, and low-calorie fruit of the Cucurbitaceae family native to South/Southeast Asia. Renowned for its cooling properties and high water content, it is popular in Ayurvedic, yogic, and culinary traditions, used in soups, stews, and the sweet candy petha.

title: Bean disease?
content: Beans are nutrient-dense seeds from the Fabaceae family, cultivated globally for human and animal consumption, offering high protein, fiber, and iron. They grow in pods on bushy or climbing plants, with common types including black, red, pinto, and green beans. Cultivated since the seventh millennium BCE, they are a vital, versatile staple.
